LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.iid_apply_of_mem_: Let t be a length-n type on a finite alphabet A, with n > 0 and empirical law r. If p is positive wherever r is positive, every word of type t has probability exp(−n[H(r) + D(r‖p)]) under n iid draws from p. Here D is discrete KL divergence on A, with every subset measurable. Both H(r) and D(r‖p) are finite and measured in nats.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.iid_toOuterMeasur: For a length-n type on a finite alphabet A with n > 0, let r be its empirical law and T its type class. If the support of r is contained in that of p, the probability of T under n iid draws from p is |T| exp(−n[H(r) + D(r‖p)]). Here D is discrete KL divergence on A, with every subset measurable. Both H(r) and D(r‖p) are finite and measured in nats.

Let r be the empirical law of a length-n type on a finite alphabet A, with n > 0. If p is positive on the support of r, the probability of the type class under n iid draws from p is at most exp(−nD(r‖p)). Here D is discrete KL divergence in nats, with every subset of A measurable.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.exp_neg_klDiv_div: Let r be the empirical law of a length-n type on a finite alphabet A, with n > 0. If p is positive on the support of r, the probability of the type class under n iid draws from p is at least exp(−nD(r‖p))/(n + 1)^|A|. Here D is discrete KL divergence in nats, with every subset of A measurable.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.iid_toOuterMeasur: Consider a length-n type on a finite alphabet, with n > 0. If a letter occurring in the type has probability zero under p, then the type class has probability zero under n iid draws from p.
